source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Dashboard"
And also enter "Server Health" -> "Sensor Reading"

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

It does not decode `_R`, map channels to physical fan assemblies and tach inputs, distinguish measured RPM from PWM target, or supply complete per-channel threshold/UI/freshness evidence.

The immediately paired `_F` family makes rear rotor/tach the stronger platform hypothesis; V3.1 records that only as presumptive and requires the fan drawing/controller specification before acceptance.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 894/2291 accepts a literal range and output presence without defining rear-rotor semantics, mapping 16 tach channels or relating RPM to fan-control state and complete UI evidence.

original_test_intent: Verify `SPD_FAN1_R` through `SPD_FAN16_R`—presumptively the rear-rotor tachometer channels of sixteen dual-rotor fan assemblies—are individually displayed in Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading with correct physical assembly/rotor identity, RPM, status and supported thresholds for the current fan-control state.
original_method: Confirm `_R` semantics, map each index to the physical fan assembly, rear rotor, tach input and controller channel, then compare complete passive raw/UI RPM fields with duty-, zone- and operating-state-specific limits while recording PWM targets, inlet temperature, system load and airflow. Preserve fan policy and logs.
manual_activity: The thermal owner confirms R as rear rotor or defines the actual suffix, maps all sixteen assemblies and controller tach channels, and supplies state-dependent RPM limits. Automation can collect passive tach/controller/UI data; a human validates physical orientation and cooling context and owns the verdict. No fan handling, PWM or airflow change is authorized.
required_inputs: Chassis/fan-board PN/revision, BMC/fan-controller build and authoritative `_R`/`_F` definitions
Fan1-16 physical assembly, thermal zone, airflow orientation, part/serial and dual-rotor construction map
Per-assembly rear-rotor tach input, pulses per revolution, controller/bus/address/channel and scaling
Stable SDR and Dashboard/Server Health identities for all rear channels
RPM units/rounding/tolerance, thresholds/hysteresis, state, polling and stale/absent rules
Current fan mode, PWM duty and target RPM per channel plus system load, inlet/ambient, altitude and airflow configuration
Acceptance for empty slots, stopped/missing rear rotor, front/rear mismatch and degraded cooling
Validated protected ipmitool/API/browser access and pinned reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or manual method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL, fan-controller, kernel or thermal logs; existing tach/fan events are relevant.
Do not issue `sensor get 'SPD_FAN1_R~SPD_FAN16_R'` as a wildcard. Enumerate sixteen exact rear-channel identities.
Do not infer R as rear solely from the letter or accept front-rotor evidence as rear coverage; confirm the controller/fan drawing and preserve the separate `_F` row.
Compare measured RPM with the contemporaneous controller target/duty and state-specific tolerance; a single static absolute RPM limit is invalid across fan modes.
Do not change fan mode/PWM, stop/remove/reseat a fan, obstruct airflow, start thermal load, alter thresholds or write the controller. These actions can compromise cooling.

Do not truncate inventory, expose passwords with `-P`, assume cipher 17 or execute the inaccessible Script. Stop without automatic retry on missing/duplicate/swapped channels, stale RPM or raw/UI/controller disagreement.
agent_execution_scope: Validate `_R`, sixteen fan/rotor/controller mappings, target, client, vendor specification and Script; build a rear-rotor expectation matrix.
Read every rear tach channel separately with full SDR/controller identity, RPM, supported thresholds, status and timestamp; capture the corresponding unchanged UI row.

Record simultaneous PWM duty/target RPM, fan mode, thermal zone, power/load, inlet/ambient and airflow, then calculate only the approved state-specific RPM tolerance and front/rear correlation needed for identity.
Preserve raw/redacted evidence and logs; perform no clear, PWM/fan/airflow/load/threshold/controller change, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve R semantics and the sixteen physical assembly/rear-rotor/tach-controller map.
Provide state-specific RPM/target tolerance, thresholds, mismatch/failure/absent and freshness rules; approve the protected read-only tool/Script.
Review all sixteen rear channels independently and issue the formal verdict without treating the front rotor, a count or an aggregate fan value as substitute coverage.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unfit as written because the range expression is not an IPMI wildcard and one response cannot prove sixteen rear-rotor channels. It omits suffix, physical rotor, controller/tach scaling and control-state context, truncates fallback data, exposes credentials and assumes cipher support.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Enumerate the sixteen rear channels, confirm physical rotor/controller identity, query each through protected read-only access, and correlate complete UI/controller RPM evidence with contemporaneous PWM targets and state-specific limits.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: SPD_FAN1_R through SPD_FAN16_R, both WebUI paths, readability/specification Criteria, generic clear text, Script URL, DeepSeek commands and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review expands the range without editing Master or manipulating fans.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a sixteen-row rear-rotor matrix keyed by physical fan assembly, rotor and controller tach channel, recording measured RPM with simultaneous PWM target/duty and thermal context, then compare complete raw/API and UI fields with state-specific tolerances.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact sixteen-fan population, dual-rotor design and BMC/fan-controller/SDR/WebUI build documented by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/fan-board, BMC/fan-controller firmware, fan PN/revision, SDR/WebUI, management client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Mechanical airflow/fan map, dual-rotor fan specification, controller tach/PWM mapping and scaling, thermal-control policy, SDR/WebUI schema and Project recipe.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Resolves the compound range into sixteen physical rear-rotor channels and adds controller target/duty and operating-state evidence while preserving passive display coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Static rear-rotor RPM does not validate front rotors, fan removal/stall detection, failover, PWM control transitions, thermal response, airflow quantity or protection behavior.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Suffix/rotor/controller map, state-specific RPM acceptance, passive synchronized timing, protected tool or reviewed Script and evidence contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Tach scaling depends on pulses per revolution, RPM changes with control mode and environment, and an alias or swapped front/rear channel can appear numerically plausible.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish/OEM or fan-controller telemetry as an approved alternative/corroboration only while preserving the original ipmitool method, recording interface/version/channel/scaling and reason, obtaining engineer approval and proving equivalent separate rear-rotor identity, RPM, threshold, status and freshness coverage. The `_F` family or aggregate fan collection is not automatically equivalent.
expected_evidence: Chassis/fan-board and BMC/controller identity plus sixteen-row physical assembly/zone/orientation/PN/serial/rear-rotor/tach-channel map
Controller/bus/address/channel, tach pulses-per-revolution/scaling and stable SDR/UI identity for every rear channel
Complete separate raw readings with RPM, threshold capabilities/values, status and synchronized timestamps plus redacted Dashboard/Server Health rows
Simultaneous PWM duty/target, fan mode, load, inlet/ambient, altitude and airflow with per-channel state-specific tolerance and any front/rear identity correlation

Explicit empty/missing/stopped/swapped/stale/mismatched disposition, pinned Script/tool evidence, no-clear/no-PWM-or-fan-or-airflow-change/no-retry proof, final cooling/BMC health and engineer-owned rear-channel verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The suffix and literal range are underdefined, but Items, UI Procedure and Criteria consistently request passive display/specification validation of sixteen `_R` fan-speed channels. Rotor/controller mapping is readiness, not a conflicting purpose.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The sixteen-channel fan-speed display purpose is clear and the paired `_F` family supports, without proving, a rear-rotor interpretation. Project fan documentation can confirm semantics and acceptance, so the review is not permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on hybrid classification while refining generic R possibilities to presumptive rear rotor based on the paired F family, still requiring Project proof.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-presence reasoning with sixteen synchronized tach/PWM/control-state and complete UI evidence.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No prior invalid draft exists for this sequence.

review_improvement: Prevents a failed range query, front rotor, aggregate fan value or tach-scaling error from being presented as sixteen rear channels, and prevents PWM/fan/airflow stimulus from being added to a passive Sensor Page test.
independent_technical_reasoning: The paired `_R` and `_F` families most plausibly represent rear and front rotors of dual-rotor fans. Meaningful RPM validation needs physical rotor identity, controller tach scaling and the simultaneous target/duty because normal RPM is state-dependent. A passive display row cannot validate stall response or authorize fan manipulation.
